#Summary1=(human1) On April 12, 2011, NASA celebrated the Space Shuttle program's 30th anniversary and upcoming final mission at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, and announced that the remaining four shuttles would be relocated to museums in New York, Washington, Los Angeles and Cape Canaveral, prompting critcism from competing sites.

#Summary2=(human2) This news article dated Wednesday, April 13 , 2011 describes the NASA ceremony held to commemorate the conclusion of the Space Shuttle Program, details the placements of four space shuttle orbiters after their final flights, and presents opposing opinions about NASA’s placement decisions for the orbiters and related space equipment.

#Summary3=(human3) Celebrating the 30 year anniversary of the first Space Shuttle launch, it is announced that the four remaining space shuttles, two of which have a flight remaining, will be permanently displayed at the Smithsonian, the Intrepid, the California Science Center, and the Kennedy Space Center, while Seattle's Museum of Flight and Houston's Johnson Space Center were not selected.

#Summary4=(human4) NASA Administrator Charles Bolden announces that NASA will display a Space Shuttle Orbiter at the Intrepid Sea-Air-Space Museum in New York, the Udvar-Hazy Center at Dulles Airport, the California Science Center, and the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex, which were chosen over competition such as Johnson Space Center in Houston and the Museum of Flight in Seattle.

#Summary5=(human5) NASA Administrator Charles Bolden announces where Space Shuttles Enterprise, Discovery, Endeavor, and Atlantis will be retired following the end of the Space Shuttle Program, in which some people were disappointed with the final location decisions.
#Text=NASA celebrates 30th anniversary of first shuttle launch ; announces new homes for retired shuttles
#Text=Wednesday , April 13 , 2011

#Text=NASA Administrator Charles Bolden announces where four space shuttle orbiters will be permanently displayed at the conclusion of the Space Shuttle Program during an event commemorating the 30th anniversay of the first shuttle launch on April 12 , 2011 .
#Text=Image : NASA Bill Ingalls .
#Text=NASA celebrated the launch of the first space shuttle Tuesday at an event at the Kennedy Space Center ( KSC ) in Cape Canaveral , Florida .
#Text=On April 12 , 1981 , Space Shuttle Columbia lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center on STS - 1 , the first space shuttle mission .

#Text=NASA held a ceremony commemorating the date outside the hangar , known as Orbiter Processing Facility - 1 , for Space Shuttle Atlantis , which is being prepped for its final mission which will be STS - 135 , which will be the last Space Shuttle mission .
#Text=At the ceremony , NASA Administrator Charles Bolden announced the locations that would be given the three remaining Space Shuttle orbiters following the end of the Space Shuttle program .

#Text=The prototype orbiter , Space Shuttle Enterprise would be relocated from the Smithsonian 's National Air and Space Museum Steven F. Udvar - Hazy Center at Washington Dulles International Airport to the Intrepid Sea - Air - Space Museum in New York City .
#Text=Space Shuttle Discovery will take the place of Enterprise at the Udvar - Hazy Center .
#Text=Discovery has already been retired following the completion of STS - 133 last month , its 39th mission .
#Text=Discovery is undergoing decommissioning and currently being prepped for display by removing toxic materials from the orbiter .
#Text=Looking back : Space Shuttle Columbia lifts off on STS - 1 from Launch Pad 39A at the Kennedy Space Center on April 12 , 1981 .
#Text=Image : NASA .

#Text=Space Shuttle Endeavour , which will launch on STS - 134 at the end of the month on April 29 , will be sent to the California Science Center in Los Angeles , California following its retirement .
#Text=Finally , Atlantis will go on display at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex following the orbiter 's last flight which launches June 28 .
#Text=Columbia was lost tragically back on February 1 , 2003 when it disintegrated during re-entry killing all seven astronauts aboard .
#Text=Space Shuttle Challenger was lost when it exploded 73 seconds after liftoff back on January 28 , 1986 killing all six aboard .
#Text=" We want to thank all of the locations that expressed an interest in one of these national treasures , " said Bolden to the gathered crowd which contained many KSC employees .
#Text=" This was a very difficult decision , but one that was made with the American public in mind .
